Implement the smallest fix within the task scope and verify all acceptance criteria.

risks.issue: The 4 failing tests in tests-green come from the round-1 change to cache_mode(). It now gates 'active' on promotion.evaluate() for every section and returns 'shadow' when there is no promotion evidence. test_pool.DisclosureCacheConfig and test_spawn.ContextTelemetry / DisclosureCachePresentation pass cfg with cache_mode='active' and no promotion state, so they now get 'shadow'. Those tests and the callers (orchestrator/spawn.py lines 73 and 417) are outside the scope list. The spec never names them, so the fix cannot make tests-green.sh exit 0 as scoped.

Hidden coupling outside scope. spawn.py calls context_router.cache_mode(cfg, 'skills') and cache_mode(cfg) on every spawn, and also in the tool_disclosure path. Adding promotion.collect/evaluate reads to that helper puts state-file I/O and a notify() call on every prompt build. A config accessor should not have side effects. Notifications will repeat per spawn while promotion is refused, and the notify call is unguarded (a failure would break spawning).

The required acceptance test, test_cache_mode_active_refuses_to_shadow_when_promotion_stays, calls cache_mode(cfg, section, root=, notify=) directly. Whichever design is chosen, the gate must stay inside cache_mode, or the test must change. That conflicts with the existing spawn/pool tests that expect the raw 'active' value. The spec does not say which side gives way, so the implementer could pick either. Also, 'promotion stays' with an empty temp root is the only case that checks the refusal. Nothing checks that refusal is silent when the mode is already shadow or off, and nothing checks notify de-duplication.

There is a silent fallback with no persisted record. When promotion is refused, cache_mode returns 'shadow' and only sends a transient notify. The decision row records the mode actually used, not that a configured 'active' was overridden. An operator reading the decision log or scorecard cannot tell a configured shadow from a refused active. Also, the section-to-feature dict lookup raises a bare KeyError for an unknown section, where the ValueError path already exists for the mode.

DisclosureCacheConfig.test_cache_mode_keys_in_tool_disclosure_and_skills iterates ('off','shadow','active') and expects the raw value back. It has to be changed or the gate has to be bypassable. tests/test_pool.py and tests/test_spawn.py are not in scope, so the spec as written forbids the necessary edit.

There is no rollback or revert note. The gate changes runtime behaviour (active silently becomes shadow) for three features. The spec should require a revert path, such as a config flag or a git revert, and a dated decisions entry.

suggested_spec_changes: Decide where the promotion gate lives. Recommended: keep cache_mode() pure (validate and return the raw config value) and add a separate effective_cache_mode(cfg, section, *, root, now, notify) in context_router.py that applies the promotion gate. Call the gated function only from the spawn sites that decide behaviour. Then the test in tests/test_context_router.py targets the new function, and the existing test_pool and test_spawn expectations stay valid without edits.

If the gate must stay inside cache_mode(), add orchestrator/spawn.py, tests/test_pool.py and tests/test_spawn.py to scope. Update those tests to mock promotion.evaluate or hermes_eval.fresh and to assert the refusal-to-shadow behaviour explicitly.
Require that the refusal notify is de-duplicated (once per feature per reason set) and wrapped so a notify failure cannot break spawn. Or move the notification to the daemon or scorecard path.
Require that a refused activation is recorded in the decision row (for example cache_mode_configured versus cache_mode_effective) so it is not a silent fallback.
Make the section-to-feature mapping raise the same ValueError for an unknown section.

Add an acceptance line that runs the four failing tests by id (test_pool.DisclosureCacheConfig, test_spawn.ContextTelemetry, test_spawn.DisclosureCachePresentation) so the fix is checked against the actual regressions, not only through tests-green.sh.
Add a rollback line: revert commit, or set cache_mode='shadow' in pool.toml, with a dated decisions.md entry.
